texts: There are over 400 different species of sharks in the world's oceans, ranging dramatically in size from the tiny dwarf lanternshark to the massive whale shark. The dwarf lanternshark is the smallest known shark species, reaching only about 8 inches in length, while the whale shark can grow up to 45 feet long and weigh up to 47,000 pounds. Sharks have been swimming in our oceans for over 420 million years, making them even older than many dinosaur species. During this time, they have evolved into highly specialized predators with unique adaptations like electroreceptors and multiple rows of regenerating teeth. Most shark species are found in tropical and temperate waters, though some species like the Greenland shark can survive in near-freezing Arctic waters and depths of up to 7,200 feet.

There are more than 400 known species of sharks, ranging dramatically in size from the tiny dwarf lanternshark to the massive whale shark. The dwarf lanternshark is one of the smallest known shark species, growing to only about 8 inches in length, while the whale shark can reach lengths of over 40 feet and weights approaching 45 tons. Modern sharks emerged about 200 million years ago and now occupy nearly every marine habitat, from shallow coastal waters to the deep ocean. Some species, like the bull shark, can even survive in freshwater rivers and lakes for extended periods. The most ancient shark fossils date back to approximately 380 million years ago, during the Late Devonian period, though these early sharks were quite different from the species we see today.
